page: Microsoft Azure E64-16s_v6 is an x86_64 memory-optimized server instance belonging to the Esv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The CPU configuration includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32.0 GB per core. The instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data shows strong performance in specific single-threaded workloads, including a Geekbench single-core score of 2115.0 and a gzip compression rate of 31.31 GB/sec. Text processing also registers in the strong tier at 2640.0. Multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks generally fall within the average range, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 15978.86 and an uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 132.03 GB/sec. For lightweight language model tasks, the server achieves a strong text generation speed of 288.15 tokens/sec on a small 135M model, though medium 7B model generation drops to an average of 12.6 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E64-16s_v6 offers high memory density relative to its compute allocation, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU processing. However, the lack of local NVMe storage means all storage operations must rely on external network-attached Premium Storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs. The absence of a GPU limits its utility for heavy parallel computing or large-scale AI training, though it supports advanced vector and matrix extensions for CPU-based acceleration.

This server configuration is designed for memory-intensive applications such as large relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, data warehousing, and enterprise applications requiring substantial RAM but moderate CPU scaling.
